To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel self-interpretable neural model that automatically extracts relevant concepts from a text and provides an explanation for a prediction in terms of the extracted concepts, while performing prediction at the same time.

we propose a self-interpretable text classification model based on the extraction of relevant concepts from the input text and we show that it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on text classification and multiclass text sentiment analysis tasks.

(i) our approach outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on the considered tasks, (ii) our approach provides relevant concepts for the task at hand, (iii) our approach is interpretable, (iv) the concepts learned are transferable to new datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of providing explanations for text processing models.

the following questions: (i) How can we build self-interpretable models for text processing that can provide an explanation of their predictions? (ii) How to automatically define the concepts to be used in the explanation without the need for human annotation?

the following questions: 1) How to define concepts that are relevant to explain the prediction task at stake? 2) How to learn a concept-based representation that is interpretable? 3) How to learn the mapping between the input and the concept-based representation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to provide explanations for text classification tasks and that it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of accuracy and interpretability.
the proposed model is capable of providing explanations for text classification and multi sentiment analysis tasks.

our model provides a new way of performing text classification, by automatically extracting concepts from the input, while being able to provide explanations of the predictions in terms of the extracted concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new model for text classification that is self-interpretable and that provides explanations in terms of concepts.
EDUCE is a self-explainable model that performs output predictions and provides explanations for the prediction in terms of the concept present in the text.
our method provides a self-interpretable approach to text processing tasks, which is able to learn concepts from raw data and provides explanations for its predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model provides a new perspective on text processing by allowing to explain the decision process in a way that can be easily understood by humans.
a model can be self-interpretable without relying on human supervision.
the model's output prediction can be explained through the presence of a small number of concept-related excerpts in the input.
